key_insight: The paper reformulates shell fracture as a mechanism-resolved phase-field model by treating the constitutive law as a certified operator over orthogonal strain invariants, enabling fibre, inter-fibre, and interaction damage channels to be modeled separately.
engineering_relevance: This makes fracture predictions for curved fibre-reinforced shells more flexible and physically interpretable, especially when curvature and fibre orientation create through-thickness asymmetry that simpler midsurface models miss.
method: Pulls Green-Lagrange strain through the shell metric Cholesky factor and decomposes it into four orthogonal invariants with exact closure.
Expresses tension-compression split, channel-wise degradation, plane-stress condensation, and consistent tangent directly in channel potentials and derivatives.
Certifies admissible operators with algebraic/solver/training-data checks, allowing either closed-form or learned constitutive laws.
evidence_signal: The approach is verified numerically on notched IM7/8552 shells, including thin and curved cases, and the results show that fibre orientation and curvature strongly affect the damage envelope and load capacity.
watch_item: The framework adds implementation complexity because admissibility, condensation, and degradation must remain consistent for each operator and curved-shell state.
paper_title: Mechanism-resolved phase-field fracture of composite shells with a certified admissible constitutive operator
